description.p: SwiftDM is a download manager for Linux with segmented HTTP/HTTPS transfers, resumable partial files, per-download bandwidth limits, an FTP path, HLS (m3u8) support and a browser integration for Chromium-based browsers.
It is a clean-room reimplementation of the behavior of a Windows download manager: no original code, assets, icons or branding are used, and it never contacts a vendor server.
Fixes the Windows installer build: a lost line break had removed a script declaration, so the installer did not compile. No application behaviour changed.

Fixes the Windows installer build of 0.22.13. The installer script did not compile, because the registry root that records the install scope used an unsupported constant; it now relies on Inno Setup's HKA root. No application behaviour changed.

The Windows installer asks whether to install for the current user or for all users. The per-user default needs no administrator rights and puts SwiftDM in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs; the all-users choice installs into Program Files and asks for elevation. Silent installs take /CURRENTUSER or /ALLUSERS, an upgrade keeps the scope of the install it replaces, and a fresh install in the other scope offers to remove the existing copy first.

Downloads whose size the server does not announce now show their transfer speed. Servers that answer without a Content-Length, FTP transfers and HLS streams all report the current rate in the Bandwidth column and in the download window, sampled over the same 200 ms window the ranged transfer uses. The remaining time stays empty for those downloads, because it needs a total size the server never sent.

The Chromium extension is now published with every release as an unpacked ZIP that installs by extracting it and choosing Load unpacked in the browser's extensions page. The archive is listed in SHA256SUMS and covered by the build provenance attestation, and the release refuses to publish when the extension ID derived from the manifest no longer matches the ID the application accepts. No CRX is published, because current browsers reject self-signed CRX files dragged onto the extensions page and Windows and macOS block local CRX installs.

SwiftDM is now a single-instance application. Starting it again from the shortcut, a terminal or the login entry brings the running window forward instead of opening a second process over the same database, and a repeated autostart stays silent so it never pops a window the user hid. A command-line download refuses to start while the application or another command-line download is running. The guard is a lock file that the kernel releases with the process, so a crash never blocks the next start.

Downloads from hosts that limit parallel connections (UploadHaven, pixeldrain and others) no longer fail with 503 after half a minute. A connection-limit refusal now costs one parallel slot instead of a retry, so the transfer settles on the number of connections the host allows and finishes; Retry-After is honoured and the documented 60 s backoff cap is applied.

A completed download can be started again from its context menu with Redownload, in the main list and inside a queue. When the file is still on disk a warning first asks to overwrite it; when it was deleted or moved the transfer starts immediately. The new file replaces the old one only after the transfer completes, so a failed redownload never destroys the previous file.

Closing the download context menu without choosing an item no longer resumes a paused row or downloads a completed one again. The menu compared its empty result with actions that only exist for some rows, so dismissing it looked like choosing Start.

Fix the Windows build of the release workflow: a header used a fixed-width integer type without including the header that declares it, which the Debian toolchain accepted but the Windows toolchain rejected. No behaviour change.

Progress updates reach the download table and the progress window every 50 ms instead of 100 ms, so the percentage, speed, and remaining-time figures move sooner without a UI timer. The speed is still smoothed over a 200 ms window so the number stays readable.

The refresh windows now read Refresh Download URL and Confirm New Download URL. The waiting window is compact, lists the file name and size, and offers Cancel; the confirmation offers Use New URL and Cancel, and paints the file-name mismatch warning in red so a wrong file is obvious.

The waiting window now disappears while the new-address confirmation is shown, and returns if the address is rejected. Duplicate download confirmations after a successful refresh are fixed: the browser handoff reply is sent before the confirmation window opens, so the extension no longer times out and retries the same capture, and a capture repeating the just-applied address is ignored for 15 seconds.

A small always-on-top window now shows which download is waiting for a refreshed address and offers Cancel Refresh. While the wait lasts, every capture from the browser is routed to the confirmation prompt and the manual New URL action is blocked with a warning, so no second download can be created before the refresh finishes.

An expired download address can be refreshed from the item context menu: SwiftDM opens the page the file came from, and the next capture of the same file from the browser replaces the dead URL, cookies and headers so the transfer resumes from the bytes already on disk instead of starting over. Only one download waits for a new address at a time.

Each category can download to its own folder, and both download dialogs can optionally stay above other windows. Download windows open at a smaller default size, the speed-limit editor fits on one row, and the category folder note no longer gets clipped.

Every download row keeps its own log file, opened from Download Properties, and the "Get File Creation Date From Server" option now sets the finished file's modification time from the HTTP Creation-Date/Last-Modified header or the FTP MDTM time. Settings loses the empty Passwords tab, and the Settings, Properties, Browser Extensions and About windows no longer block the Download Complete and progress windows.

The Windows GUI executable uses the GUI subsystem, so launching it from Explorer, a shortcut or autostart opens no console window, and the executable together with the Inno Setup installer carries the SwiftDM application icon.
The experimental Windows 10 port ships from main with a portable ZIP and a per-user Inno Setup installer, and release tags publish both next to the Debian package.
Completed queue items no longer open the global Download Complete window or the download folder; a queue uses its own per-item notification instead.
The Download Confirmation window asks which queue a download belongs to when several queues exist, instead of silently using the first one.
Named download queues with independent scheduling, limits, notifications and shutdown. Selecting the Queues branch shows a queue overview and switches the toolbar to queue mode.
The Download Properties window groups its read-only values into General, Location, Source and Time sections. The Download progress and Download Confirmation windows use the same section layout.
The toolbar Resume and Stop buttons follow the selected download states, and the toolbar has dividers after New URL and Stop.
The settings window groups its options into labeled sections on every tab.
The download confirmation appears while file metadata is checked, and the initial transfer reuses the probe instead of repeating it.
The General tab of the settings window can switch the download confirmation dialog off; the downloads then start automatically.
The message boxes of the app use their own icons: information, warning, question and completion.
New application icon; the launcher icons are rendered from the icon source during the build.
The Quit button in the toolbar uses the power icon.
The General tab of the settings window offers a tray icon switch, a close-to-tray switch and an option that opens the download folder when a transfer finishes.
New Interface tab in the settings window: toolbar size, toolbar text, a light, dark or system theme and a simple or colorful tray icon. The changes apply right away.
The configuration file is split into one section per settings tab; older configuration files keep working.
The settings window is split into five tabs: General, Interface, Download, Proxy/Socks and Passwords.
The download confirmation window keeps a fixed size and shows the file size on its own row.
The Debian package no longer pulls a browser and printer stack; browser integration remains optional.
SwiftDM starts silently in the system tray when launched at login; the main window is no longer shown at startup.
Missing downloaded files are shown only in the download list; the file-not-found warning appears when the user opens the file.
Fix downloads whose URL paths contain spaces, including Google Drive folder ZIPs.
Quit actions ask for confirmation before closing the application completely.
Browser download confirmation no longer restores the main window when it is hidden or minimized.
Speed limit toggle and value can be changed while a download is in progress. Other download options remain editable when paused.
Speed limiter with an enable toggle, preset values and an active-limit display next to the bandwidth value.
Confirm every download before it starts: file name and size, category and location, with Download Now and Cancel.
Restore the download list from the SQLite history at startup, including paused and failed rows.
Installable build: CMake install rules and a Debian package.
